name: sha1
title: Calculate a SHA1 hash of an object

origin.description: Hash an object so the result is the same on 32-bit and 64-bit systems. Floating-point values are reduced with digits and zapsmall before hashing.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The object to hash. Dispatch follows the class.

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Approximate significant digits in base 10. The default is 14, and 4 for anova.

arguments.name: zapsmall
arguments.text: Values smaller than about 10^-zapsmall become 0. The default is 7.
Passed on. environment = FALSE drops the environment of a function or formula.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: The digest algorithm. The default is sha1.

origin.details: Numbers are written with num2hex, then hashed. Attributes are included at package version 0.6.23 and later, and srcref is ignored from 0.6.24. The manual has no example; the captured call is sha1(c(1, 2, 3)).

translation.description: Hash an object after the same numeric reduction sha1 uses, then call digest.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A real vector is c(1, 2, 3). Use real(), integer(), character(), data_frame(), and the other constructors for the matching R types.

arguments.name: digits
arguments.text: Significant digits. The default is 14, and 4 for an anova object.

arguments.name: algo
arguments.text: Passed to digest. The default is sha1.

arguments.name: kwargs
arguments.text: environment=False drops a function or formula environment.

translation.details: The package version is 0.6.39, so attributes are kept and srcref is dropped. A repeated symbol in the serialization is a four-byte reference.
translation.example:
from digest import real, sha1
print(sha1(real([1, 2, 3])))
